h: A Family Race Day in South London
p: Mitcham makes a good base for a family day out in this corner of south London. Karting suits older kids and teenagers best, though junior drivers have to meet minimum age and height rules, so check those before booking to avoid disappointment on the day.

Make a proper day of it by pairing the race with somewhere for the younger ones. Deen City Farm, near Morden Hall Park, is a community farm where children can meet the animals. Mitcham Common is a big open space for kite-flying and runarounds, and it's a great spot to burn off any leftover energy.
If you're travelling in, the Tramlink connects Mitcham with Croydon and Wimbledon, so it's easy to get around without a car. Trains to central London run from nearby stations too.

On the track, the best advice for first-timers is to stay smooth and look ahead. Brake before each corner, not halfway round it, and feed the power back in gently as you come out of the bend. Lap times drop quickly once you get the hang of it.
Bring a bottle of water too, because it gets surprisingly warm under a helmet.

Plan food for afterwards, and make sure everyone has flat, closed shoes and clothes they can move in. Leave plenty of time to arrive and sign in, because sessions start on time and late arrivals can miss out on their race.
